phase: PHASE-03 - GPWCF Framework Filesystem & Package Architecture
purpose: Define actual dependency ownership and direction, installation profiles, and the supported Core and Prefect Integration Public APIs before finalizing the GPWCF filesystem architecture.

scope.referenceConsumerRole: Genericity/conformance reference only; Generator-specific stages, steps, contracts, dependencies and policies remain consumer-owned.
exclusions: No implementation or filesystem movement beyond the separately authorized package-marker skeleton.
No specialized contract is modified or generalized here.
No Prefect adoption reconsideration; Prefect 3.9.2 remains accepted.
The 106-package Prefect snapshot is not the minimal runtime dependency closure.
Wave 1-6 detailed design proposals remain draft until separately accepted; their selected designs do not silently change this baseline.

governingDecisions.decision: Core has no third-party runtime dependency in the current baseline; its declared Python runtime dependency baseline is the Python standard library only.
Prefect is an opt-in dependency of the separate Prefect Integration package/surface, never a dependency of Core.
The accepted initial Prefect runtime requirement is prefect==3.9.2, aligned with CPython 3.15.1 x64 on Windows x64 for the qualified profile.
The complete transitive Prefect dependency lock must be derived and verified from a clean isolated Integration environment; the captured 106-package environment is evidence/snapshot only.

The existing SMRB .dependencies and shared .env arrangement remains the solution-level development dependency-management mechanism; GPWCF must not create a parallel local dependency bundle or environment.
Core Public API and Prefect Integration Public API are separate explicit supported contract boundaries; neither is merely an __init__.py re-export convenience.
Optional Supporting Unit patterns are opt-in and must not become transitive mandatory imports or installation dependencies for consumers that do not select them.
Generator dependencies, including pygccxml, remain consumer-owned and must not enter Core or Prefect Integration declarations without a separately demonstrated and approved need.

runtimeAndPackagingBaseline.supportPolicy: CPython 3.15.1 x64 / Windows x64 is the currently evidenced baseline. Do not publish a broader Python-version or platform compatibility range until Core and Integration are tested against an explicit support matrix.

logicalPackages.name: GPWCF Core
logicalPackages.installation: Install/use without Prefect or any workflow runtime.
logicalPackages.runtimeDependencies: Python standard library only in the current baseline.

logicalPackages.name: GPWCF Prefect Integration
logicalPackages.installation: Install only when a consumer chooses the accepted Prefect integration.
logicalPackages.runtimeDependencies: Prefect 3.9.2 plus its resolved transitive runtime closure.

runtimeAndPackagingBaseline.packageRelationship: Prefect Integration depends inward on Core Public API. Core has no reverse dependency, optional import, or installation requirement for Prefect Integration.

distributionMechanism.rule: The logical Core and Prefect Integration boundaries remain separate. Installing the base distribution must not install or import Prefect; selecting the prefect extra installs Prefect Integration requirements only.
distributionMechanism.optionalExtraAlternative: Accepted for the initial release as the chosen distribution shape, subject to clean Core-only and Core-plus-Integration installation tests.
distributionMechanism.openChoice: None for the initial distribution shape; build backend and build-system pinning remain a separate release gate.
distributionMechanism.decision: Select Option A for the initial release: one GPWCF distribution with Core as the dependency-free base and Prefect Integration exposed through an optional prefect extra.
distributionMechanism.buildBackend: Deferred; select and pin before producing build artifacts.

prefectDependencyQualification.adoptionDecision: Accepted and settled: Prefect 3.9.2 is the initial pinned external workflow runtime under ADR-GPWCF-PREFECT-001.

environmentEvidence.interpretation: Complete environment snapshot including packages not required by the minimal PoC; not a minimized Integration lock or proof all 106 packages are required.

deploymentDependenciesNotPackageBaseDepe: SQLite persistence used by qualified local profile
Process Worker processes and work pool
prefectDependencyQualification.qualifiedOperationalProfile: Windows x64, CPython 3.15.1, Prefect 3.9.2, local SQLite API server, Process Work Pool, two Process Workers with flow-run limit 1, two Stage deployments.
qualificationBoundary: PHASE-01 qualified native Flow hierarchy, task fan-out/fan-in and identity correlation with fixtures; production GPWCF binding was not tested.
PHASE-02 qualified same-host two-Process-Worker sibling Stage overlap, synthetic parent linkage and Stage domain-result retrieval across five repeated runs.

Not qualified: multi-host code distribution/storage, more than two concurrent Stages, production GPWCF binding, failure/cancellation/timeout/retry/worker-loss recovery, safe settlement, sibling Step concurrency and production throughput/resource sizing.
requiredBeforeRelease: Create a clean isolated environment for Integration only.
Install exact direct requirement prefect==3.9.2 and capture resolver-produced transitive closure.
Separate runtime packages from PoC/developer/test/documentation/optional-service packages using clean imports and profile-specific tests.
Record exact versions and hashes in a reproducible lock; review licenses and Python/platform markers.
Prove Core install/import with Prefect absent and Integration import/run with locked Prefect environment.
Do not add optional API-server database backends, distributed queues, cloud services or worker infrastructure unless the chosen deployment profile explicitly requires them.

publicApiArchitecture.principle: Public API is the stable supported consumer contract boundary. Public status is explicit and versioned; internal module importability does not make a module public.

surfaces.name: Core Public API
surfaces.purpose: Expose generic framework Entities, callable contracts, typed result contracts and approved consumer specialization points.

contractGroups.exposure: Stage Entity identity and only generic Stage contracts actually established. Dedicated Stage callable contract remains a known gap; do not invent a signature or claim a complete Stage invocation API before GAP-STAGE-CALLABLE-001 is resolved.
Step identity, Stage-facing callable contract, Step specialization points and StepExecutionResult contract.
SPU callable contract, SPU identity and SPUExecutionResult contract.
Separate opt-in contract sub-surfaces for Error Handling, Validation and Observation; import only the selected pattern.
Only generic primitives demonstrated by the contract inventory. No generic FlowResult, universal Error Model, SupportingUnit base or shared manager is inferred.

Compose Stage/Step entities through public contract boundaries
Use typed SPU and Step result contracts
Opt into a supported Supporting Pattern contract

Consumer-specific business models and Generator Stage/Step models
Internal composition collaborators unless explicitly promoted
Unapproved generic Stage callable signature or universal Stage Flow Result schema

surfaces.name: Prefect Integration Public API
surfaces.availability: Explicit opt-in; requires GPWCF Core and Prefect 3.9.2 integration runtime.
surfaces.purpose: Expose supported entry points for binding GPWCF public functional contracts and hierarchy to Prefect-native Flow, Deployment, Subflow and Task execution.

contractGroups.exposure: Supported binding declarations/adapters for Stage, Step, SPU and selected Supporting Unit contracts to permitted Prefect executable elements.
Supported invocation boundary for Stage Parent Flow/Deployment and nested Step Subflow while preserving the Step callable boundary.
Typed mapping of GPWCF domain identities/invocation context to Prefect operational IDs without conflation.
Mapping of native execution outcomes/evidence to GPWCF domain result and exception contracts without replacing either with Prefect State.
Only integration-owned configuration required for the selected Prefect profile; no universal scheduler/adapter abstraction.

consumerCapabilities: Bind consumer-defined callable implementations to native Prefect elements through documented contracts
Invoke supported Stage integration boundary once callable contract is resolved
Read operational correlation separately from GPWCF domain results
exclusions: Core Entity ownership or domain semantics
Consumer business logic or Generator decomposition
Direct dependency on private Integration internals
Universal workflow adapter, plugin manager, scheduler or registry
Unqualified deployment capabilities presented as supported guarantees

namespaceAndImportPolicy.status: Logical public namespace decisions for architecture; concrete Python package paths/export files are finalized in Filesystem_Architecture.
namespaceAndImportPolicy.internalNamespaces: Internal implementation modules live outside public_api and are not stable consumer import targets.
namespaceAndImportPolicy.facadeRule: Public API modules explicitly expose approved symbols from internal modules; the supported contract is the public_api module itself, not an implementation module or blanket re-export.
namespaceAndImportPolicy.versioningRule: Public contracts and supported imports are versioned; incompatible removal/renaming/semantics require explicit compatibility/deprecation policy.
namespaceAndImportPolicy.optionalImportRule: Importing gpwcf.public_api.core must not import Prefect or load optional Supporting Pattern implementations. Integration imports Prefect only within its opt-in boundary. Optional patterns load only when explicitly imported/selected.
namespaceAndImportPolicy.noPrivateImportsRule: Consumers must not rely on internal paths, private helpers or incidental re-exports.

readinessGaps.impact: Stage identity/role can be represented, but callable signature and complete invocation contract cannot be finalized without a separate Stage contract decision.
Stage-specific Flow Result remains a Stage specialization; do not define a universal public FlowResult schema.
StepExecutionResult is public and mandatory, but optional specialized slots require approved lazy/opaque/protocol typing that does not import every optional pattern.
Generator Common Error Model and dependent Step error model remain outside baseline Core Public API.
Publication specialization is exposed only through selected Error Handling contract; concrete policy remains consumer-owned.

publicApiArchitecture.status: Conceptual Core and optional Prefect Integration boundaries accepted. Exact exports and public_api source package files remain gated by explicit acceptance of the Wave 6 Public API design and its reconciliation.
publicApiArchitecture.materializationGate: Do not create src/gpwcf/public_api package markers or export symbols while .docs/00.00_Primary_Architecture/Public_API/16.00_Public_API_Architecture.json remains draft-for-architecture-review.

developmentBuildAndVerificationDependenc.principle: Development/build/test/verification tools are not runtime dependencies unless the shipped package imports or executes them at runtime.

currentEvidence.testTooling: No GPWCF-specific third-party test/build/type-check dependency is declared in the reviewed GPWCF requirements file; do not invent one here.

verificationProfiles.requirements: Core only, no Prefect or Generator dependencies; verify import graph and Core Public API.
Core plus one selected optional pattern at a time; verify unselected patterns are not imported/required.

externalServicesAndOperationalDependenci.principle: External runtime services and deployment processes are distinct from Python package dependencies. They are provisioned by the selected deployment profile, not silently installed as Core prerequisites.
externalServicesAndOperationalDependenci.qualificationCaveat: Current qualification is a same-host two-worker profile. Multi-host distribution/storage, higher Stage concurrency and failure/recovery remain open technical qualifications; they do not alter the settled Prefect adoption decision.

dependencyAndImportInvariants: Core runtime imports are standard-library-only in the current baseline.
Core Public API import succeeds in an environment where Prefect is not installed.
Importing Core does not import integrations.prefect or any Prefect package.
Prefect Integration imports Core only through Core Public API, not Core internals.
Prefect imports remain within the opt-in Integration boundary.
Optional Supporting Pattern APIs are separately importable and not eagerly imported by Core root or Step result module.
Step Composition consumes only selected Supporting Pattern contract surfaces; pattern modules do not import Step Composition implementation.
No consumer or Generator code is imported by Core or Integration.
No Generator Common Error Model, pygccxml or Generator extraction engine is installed by Core or Integration.
No generic shared_contracts package is created until a real reusable contract and dependency closure are established.
No package imports Prefect State as a substitute for SPUExecutionResult, StepExecutionResult or Stage Flow Result.
The Public API surface, not private implementation paths, is the compatibility boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Core and Prefect Integration have separate dependency ownership and independently usable installation profiles.
Core has no third-party runtime dependency in the current baseline and imports without Prefect installed.
Prefect 3.9.2 is the accepted pinned initial Integration runtime; its closure is not conflated with the 106-package environment snapshot.
The shared SMRB .dependencies/.env arrangement is reused for solution development; no parallel GPWCF dependency bundle is created.
Generator pygccxml and other consumer dependencies remain consumer-owned.
Development/build/test/verification dependencies are distinguished from published runtime dependencies.
Core Public API and Prefect Integration Public API are explicit, separately owned and versioned contract boundaries.
Optional Supporting Pattern imports/installations remain opt-in and isolated.
Stage callable, optional result typing, generic error model and Stage Flow Result gaps remain explicit; no missing contracts are invented.
Dependency directions preserve Entity/Aggregate ownership and introduce no generic Root, shared-contract package, scheduler, adapter or manager without evidence.
The initial distribution shape is one distribution with a genuinely optional Prefect extra; build backend selection remains separate.
SMRB/.dependencies/ is the solution-level external dependency/source-asset location; SMRB/.env/ remains the shared Python virtual environment; no GPWCF-local duplicate store is created.
